extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians (especially graduate students and early-career researchers) seeking career/research advice
extracted.subtask_description: Advice for conducting mathematical research and producing high-quality mathematical writing through disciplined work habits (reading, writing, thinking) rather than relying on flashes of genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard work over genius
rubrics_metrics.description: "Mathematical breakthroughs are not powered solely (or even primarily) by 'Eureka' moments of genius, but are in fact largely a product of hard work."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations and self-assessments should privilege sustained effort and steady progress over waiting for or celebrating isolated flashes of inspiration. Avoid the anti-pattern of expecting single 'genius' events to carry projects to completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading, writing, and thinking together
rubrics_metrics.description: Success requires literature engagement, written drafts, and deep thought — not contemplation alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Productive research combines careful reading of literature, iterative written sketches and drafts, and focused thinking. One should not rely solely on passive contemplation; producing written work (notes, drafts) is integral to developing ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master the details
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding demands reading all relevant literature and writing detailed sketches and complete treatments, not only grasping grand concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not stop at high-level intuition: read relevant papers thoroughly, write detailed sketches, and produce complete treatments when appropriate. Superficial understanding of details is a weakness; mastery is shown by working through technical parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build foundational knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress requires learning and relearning the field, understanding tool strengths and limitations, staying informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest time in acquiring and refreshing background material. Be aware of what techniques can and cannot do; keep up with the literature so your toolkit remains relevant. Treat foundational learning as an ongoing, necessary part of research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality over quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Forcing oneself to work even when one is tired, unmotivated, unprepared, or distracted" becomes counterproductive. Focused hours beat numerous distracted hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise productive, focused work sessions rather than maximising raw hours. Recognise diminishing returns: tired or distracted work often wastes time. Schedule work to maximize concentration and effectiveness instead of enforcing arbitrary hour quotas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enjoy your work to sustain effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Enjoy your work to sustain effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intrinsic enjoyment helps maintain long-term disciplined effort. Seek aspects of research you find rewarding so that sustained work feels feasible and less draining; if enjoyment is absent, reassess projects or approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think strategically ahead rather than obsessing over single problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Think strategically ahead rather than obsessing over single problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan research directions and consider broader strategy (which problems to pursue, which tools to develop) instead of becoming fixated on one particular problem to the exclusion of all else. Strategic thinking helps allocate effort where it is most likely to pay off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain multiple projects to prevent burnout
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain multiple projects to prevent burnout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep several projects at different stages so you can switch when stuck or fatigued on one, reducing the risk of burnout and increasing chances of continual progress across areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise when projects need modification or abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise when projects need modification or abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly evaluate progress and be willing to change direction or drop projects that are no longer productive. Persistence is valuable, but so is pragmatism in reallocating effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish productive work from merely maximising work hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish productive work from merely maximising work hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge research by the quality and progress produced, not by hours logged. Seek indicators of productive momentum (progress on drafts, solved subproblems, clarified ideas) rather than counting time as a proxy for value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math writing quality reflects sustained disciplined effort
rubrics_metrics.description: A piece of math writing of "good" quality reflects sustained, disciplined effort across reading + writing + thinking, not flash insight alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing mathematical exposition or research output, give weight to evidence of sustained work: thorough literature engagement, multiple drafts, and careful argumentation. Treat polished writing and complete treatments as signals of underlying disciplined effort.
